top_story.headline: ActBlue tells the FEC it now processes contributions from donors with foreign addresses
top_story.dek: A Form 99 filed October 22 says a passport-verification update let U.S. citizens living abroad give through the platform starting around October 2.
paragraphs: ActBlue told the FEC in a one-page Form 99 that, beginning on or about 10/02/2026 and following an update to its passport-verification process, it began processing contributions from donors with addresses outside the United States. The filing says these are contributions from U.S. citizens residing abroad and that they will appear on ActBlue's regular reports with the donor's foreign address as provided. (Form 99)
The filing does not say how many foreign-address contributions have been processed, their dollar value, or which committees received them. It was received 10/22, two days before this edition.

Also filed 10/22: the Harris County Democratic Party told the FEC that $102,999.17 in state-designated fundraising receipts was mistakenly deposited into its federal account and is being moved to the state account. (Form 99)

sections.headline: FEC sends 53 notices to candidate committees, nearly all over the Pre-General Report
paragraphs: All 53 letters are dated October 23 and went to candidate committees. 51 reference the Pre-General Report (10/01/2026 to 10/14/2026), and the standard frame says the committee may have failed to file it. Two reference the October Quarterly Report. No letter in this batch carries dollar figures or itemized questions in the text provided. Two committees, Ahsen for Virginia and the Campaign Committee for Greg Stoker, received two letters each. No response due dates appear in the text provided.

sections.headline: ActBlue's foreign-address disclosure and a Texas county party's misdeposit lead 28 Form 99s
paragraphs: Most of the 28 Form 99s are short statements from small committees saying they are under the $5,000 reporting threshold. A handful are substantive: ActBlue on foreign-address donors, the Harris County Democratic Party on state money deposited in its federal account, and the Ohio Democratic Party - Federal answering an FEC letter. Several were received October 21 or 22, one to three days before this edition.

items: ActBlue tells the FEC it began processing contributions from donors with addresses outside the United States around October 2. The filing ties this to an update to its passport-verification process and says the donors are U.S. citizens living abroad. Their foreign addresses will show on its regular reports. Received 10/22. (Form 99)

The Harris County Democratic Party tells the FEC that $102,999.17 in state-designated receipts was mistakenly deposited into its federal account. The filing explains its October 1-14 Pre-General Form 3X: 36 receipts are being corrected through transfers to the state account, and the total includes $4,500 in checks deposited October 1, among them a $2,500 contribution from Rodney Ellis. It reports a $14,985 corrective transfer for a $15,000 September 'Auntie Up AAPI' receipt less a $15 bank fee, and says a $14,000 Bayou City Event Center payment was for a party-sponsored event and not an in-kind candidate contribution. Received 10/22. (Form 99)

The Ohio Democratic Party - Federal answers an FEC letter dated September 16 about its August Monthly report. It says it amended its July Monthly report to correct ending cash on hand and amended its statement of organization to add the DSCC Victory Fund and Friends of State Parties. It says its Consulting/Communications payments were consulting fees, not public communications, and its printing payments did not refer to a clearly identified federal candidate. Received 10/21. (Form 99)

McGinnis for the People tells the FEC it emailed 420 donors on October 22 asking for their profession and employer. The Donorbox-database donors were missing that information, and the committee says responses have started coming in. Treasurer is Frederick Clarkson. Received 10/22. (Form 99)

Matt Castelli for Congress asks the FEC to accept a Form 99 in place of its Pre-General report. The New York Democratic challenger committee says it filed a termination report October 15 and had no activity from 10/01 to 10/14. Treasurer Victoria Perrone also signed the Riley Gendebien Victory Fund filing below. Received 10/22. (Form 99)

The Riley Gendebien Victory Fund asks the FEC to accept a Form 99 in place of its Pre-General report. It says it filed a termination report October 15 and had no activity from 10/01 to 10/14. It shares treasurer Victoria Perrone and a Washington mailing address with Matt Castelli for Congress. Received 10/22. (Form 99)

RJTS2028, a Republican presidential committee, changes its filing frequency to monthly and describes a $150 million donation. The filing says the money came from RJTS News USA for press materials and ads from September 4 to October 14. The filing offers no supporting documentation, and the claim is unverified. Candidate is Roland Jackson. (Form 99)

Friends for Michael Smith, the Nevada open-seat House committee, files a Form 99 titled 'Loan Forgiveness'. The page has no text beyond the committee's name and address, so the PDF text gives no details. Received 10/22. (Form 99)

Ethan Agarwal for Congress files an FEC Form 1 statement of organization under a Form 99 label. The Democratic House challenger committee in California's 17th District names the candidate as treasurer and is dated 10/23. The scan is poorly readable. (Form 99)

Jason Clark US Congress files a paper Form 3 report that is largely illegible. The Republican Colorado House challenger committee's scan is handwritten, and the figures could not be read reliably from the PDF. (Form 99)

Michael DeName for US President sends a handwritten submission the PDF text cannot read. The presidential committee's three-page scan is stamped October 23, and nothing in the text layer is legible. (Form 99)
Raglan LLC Corp PAC tells the FEC it made no financial contributions in its Q3 2026 period. The filing says $0 was exchanged from August 3 to September 30. (Form 99)
Quince PAC tells the FEC its activity did not exceed the registration threshold from October 1 to 14. Received 10/22. (Form 99)

Antoine Kelley for Congress tells the FEC it is not required to file its October 22 Pre-General report. The Georgia independent challenger committee says it has not exceeded the statutory threshold. (Form 99)
Ashley Webb: Take No Prisoners says it is under $5,000 for both the Q3 and 12-Day Pre-General periods. The Maine Democratic Senate challenger committee filed for the public record. (Form 99)
Ayden Scott for Congress says its campaign has not raised or spent $5,000. The Utah House challenger committee filed one sentence. (Form 99)

A shared vendor is a coordination-risk flag, not proof: FEC rules allow common vendors behind a firewall. Generic platforms (ActBlue, Google, postal, banks, broadcasters) are excluded.

apod.title: Rosetta's Selfie
apod.caption: This Rosetta spacecraft selfie was snapped on October 7th, 2014. At the time the comet-chasing spacecraft was about 472 million kilometers from planet Earth, but only 16 kilometers from the surface of comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko.
